title: Oven-Roasted Turkish Honey Kunefe
description: A sweet, flaky pastry dessert featuring honey as the main sweetener, inspired by Turkish cuisine. This recipe uses a low-glycemic-friendly alternative to traditional sugar, perfect for a healthy dessert option.
instructions: Combine milk, yeast, and sugar substitute in a large mixing bowl. Let it sit for 5 minutes, until yeast is activated.
Add melted butter, honey, and cinnamon. Mix well until all ingredients are combined.
Gradually add kunefe cheese (or phyllo dough) and mix until dough is formed.
Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes, until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover it with a damp cloth, and let it rise in a warm place for 1 hour, until doubled in size.
Punch down the dough and divide it into 2-3 equal pieces. Roll out each piece into a thin sheet, about 1/8 inch thick.
Cut the sheets into 1-inch wide strips.
Coil the strips into a spiral shape and place them in a copper pot.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the pastry is golden brown and crispy.
While the pastry is baking, combine mirin, water, and melted ghee in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil and then reduce the heat to low.
Simmer for 5-7 minutes, or until the mixture has thickened slightly.
Remove the pastry from the oven and brush the mirin glaze all over it.
If using walnuts, sprinkle them on top of the pastry before serving.
